title: Gunn et al. v. Covenant Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC held that Covenant Presbytery did not err by receiving and acting on its MNA Committee’s report and recommendations; Gunn’s complaint was denied, with no corrective relief ordered.
first_summary: Ministers challenged Covenant Presbytery’s receipt of and action on its MNA Committee report concerning the Mississippi Joint Committee on Campus Work, arguing that the committee exceeded its assigned authority. The SJC denied the complaint because the study extended the assigned salary inquiry, the committee had oversight responsibility for MJCCW, its recommendations proposed discussion rather than structural change, and Presbytery had ruled the matters properly before it.
summary: Ministers challenged Covenant Presbytery’s receipt of and action on its MNA Committee report concerning the Mississippi Joint Committee on Campus Work, contending that the committee exceeded its assigned authority. The SJC denied the complaint. It held that the study naturally extended the salary inquiry, the committee had oversight of MJCCW, the recommendations sought discussion rather than structural change, and Presbytery had ruled the matters properly before it. The record could not establish claimed traditional limits on oversight, and no corrective relief issued.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2011-04 is Grover Gunn et al. v. Covenant Presbytery; it was combined with identical Case 2011-03 and heard by an expanded panel. The full SJC adopted the amended reasoning. Printed pp. 554, 557, 560; lines 15, 51–61, 97.
evidence_notes.dispute: The issue was whether Presbytery erred by receiving and acting on its MNA Committee’s report and recommendations concerning MJCCW. Printed p. 557; lines 63–65.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The complaints were denied because the study extended the salary inquiry, MNA-CP had MJCCW oversight, the recommendations sought discussion rather than structural change, and Presbytery ruled the matters properly before it. Printed pp. 557–560; lines 67–69, 91–95.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC said the record could not establish respondents’ assertions about the traditional scope of oversight and treated Presbytery as best positioned to judge conformity with its wishes. Printed p. 560; line 93.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference; the Moderator’s ruling and Presbytery vote were procedural history considered in the reasoning. Printed pp. 556, 559; lines 31–49, 91.

source_limits: The supplied opinion adjudicates Cases 2011-03 and 2011-04 together and describes their complaints as identical; it does not separately reproduce Gunn’s complete pleading or enumerate additional specifications.
